html:
The Muniche were a small people of the village of Munichis, about 16 kilometres west of Yurimaguas, in the Loreto region of the Peruvian Amazon. Their language was an isolate, related to no other known language.

Jesuit missionaries of the Mainas missions gathered them into a mission town in the 1600s. Over the centuries they shifted to Spanish and Quechua. The language was already dying by the 1930s, and its last fluent speaker died in the late 1990s. Neighbours: Shawi and Chamicuro. See Peru.
